**Serves** {{< meta servings >}} · **Active** {{< meta active-time >}} · **Total** {{< meta total-time >}}

A long, slow rise does the work that kneading normally would, and baking in a
preheated covered pot traps steam for a crackly crust. Mix it the night before
and bake it the next afternoon.

## Ingredients

- 400 g (3 cups) bread flour, plus more for dusting
- 8 g (1½ tsp) kosher salt
- 1 g (¼ tsp) instant yeast
- 300 ml (1¼ cups) cool water

## Method

1. Stir the flour, salt, and yeast together in a large bowl. Add the water and
   mix with a spoon until no dry flour remains. The dough will be shaggy and
   sticky.
2. Cover and leave at room temperature for 12–18 hours, until the surface is
   dotted with bubbles and the dough has more than doubled.
3. Turn the dough onto a well-floured counter. Fold the edges into the middle a
   few times to form a rough ball, then flip it seam-side down onto a floured
   tea towel or piece of parchment.
4. Cover and let rise for 1–2 hours, until it holds a fingerprint that springs
   back slowly.
5. About 45 minutes before baking, put a lidded Dutch oven in the oven and heat
   to 230 °C (450 °F).
6. Carefully tip the dough into the hot pot, seam-side up. Cover and bake for
   30 minutes.
7. Remove the lid and bake another 15–20 minutes, until the crust is deep brown
   and the loaf sounds hollow when tapped underneath.
8. Cool on a rack for at least 1 hour before cutting.

## Notes

- Parchment makes the transfer into the hot pot much less nerve-racking: lower
  the dough in by the paper and leave it there.
- Swap up to 100 g of the flour for whole wheat; add an extra tablespoon of
  water if you do.
- In a cold kitchen the first rise can take the full 18 hours or more. Go by
  the bubbles, not the clock.
